subject: Biology
description: Vitamins — fat-soluble (ADEK), water-soluble (B-complex, C); deficiency diseases, sources, daily requirements, nutritional schemes.

questions.explanation: VITAMIN A DEFICIENCY → NIGHT BLINDNESS (nyctalopia — difficulty seeing in dim light) → can progress to XEROPHTHALMIA (dry eyes) → BLINDNESS if severe. VITAMIN A — chemical name RETINOL. KEY ROLE: forms RHODOPSIN (visual pigment in retinal rods); essential for low-light vision. ALSO: skin health, immune function, growth. SOURCES: liver, fish-liver oils, egg yolk, dairy. PLANT precursor: BETA-CAROTENE (orange-red pigment) → converted to vitamin A in body. Carotene-rich: CARROTS, SPINACH, SWEET POTATO, MANGO, PAPAYA, RED PEPPERS, PUMPKIN. INDIA — VITAMIN A DEFICIENCY: major public-health problem. ~50% Indian children < 5 years had subclinical Vit A deficiency (NFHS-5). LEADING preventable CAUSE of childhood blindness globally. NATIONAL VITAMIN A SUPPLEMENTATION programme: high-dose Vit A drops to children every 6 months. RECENT — GOLDEN RICE: GM rice biofortified with beta-carotene (developed by Ingo Potrykus + Peter Beyer); approved in Bangladesh + Philippines, INDIA still debating. KEY VITAMIN-DEFICIENCY DISEASES (memorize!): (1) VIT A — Night blindness, Xerophthalmia. (2) VIT B1 (thiamine) — BERIBERI. (3) VIT B2 (riboflavin) — CHEILOSIS, glossitis. (4) VIT B3 (niacin) — PELLAGRA. (5) VIT B6 (pyridoxine) — anemia. (6) VIT B9 (folate) — neural-tube defects in fetus, megaloblastic anemia. (7) VIT B12 — pernicious anemia. (8) VIT C (ascorbic acid) — SCURVY. (9) VIT D — RICKETS (children), OSTEOMALACIA (adults). (10) VIT E — sterility, hemolysis (rare). (11) VIT K — bleeding tendency. UPSC angle: nutrition + public health policy. PYQ FREQUENCY: vitamin-deficiency in NEET, NCERT, SSC GA 1-2× per paper.

questions.stem: SCURVY is caused by deficiency of:
questions.explanation: SCURVY — deficiency of VITAMIN C (ASCORBIC ACID). SYMPTOMS: bleeding gums, loosening of teeth, slow wound healing, joint pain, weakness, fatigue, anemia, skin bruising. EXTREME cases (~3 months without Vit C): can be fatal. HISTORICAL: SCURVY was a 'SAILOR's DISEASE' on long voyages (no fresh fruits). KILLED ~2 MILLION sailors (1500-1800). JAMES LIND (Scottish physician, 1747) — first controlled clinical trial: showed citrus fruits CURE scurvy. By late 1700s, British Royal Navy issued LEMON/LIME juice to sailors → 'LIMEYS' nickname. NOBEL: ALBERT SZENT-GYÖRGYI (1937) for isolating Vit C from paprika. VITAMIN C — chemical name: ASCORBIC ACID (Latin 'a' = without + 'scorbutus' = scurvy). RDA (adult): 75-90 mg/day; smokers + pregnancy more. SOURCES (rich): CITRUS fruits (oranges, lemons, lime), GUAVA (very high — 200+ mg per fruit!), AMLA (Indian gooseberry — exceptionally high; 600 mg/100g!), strawberry, kiwi, papaya, tomato, capsicum, broccoli. KEY ROLES of Vit C: (1) COLLAGEN synthesis — connective tissue, skin, blood vessels. (2) ANTIOXIDANT. (3) IRON ABSORPTION enhancement (eat Vit C with iron-rich foods!). (4) Immune function. (5) HEALING. WATER-SOLUBLE — not stored well; need DAILY intake. Excess EXCRETED in urine. INDIA: Vit C deficiency relatively rare due to varied diet; AMLA-based products (Chyavanprash) traditional. UPSC angle: malnutrition + Anemia Mukt Bharat 2018. PYQ FREQUENCY: scurvy in NEET, NCERT, SSC GA 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: RICKETS in children is caused by deficiency of:
questions.explanation: RICKETS (children) + OSTEOMALACIA (adults) = Vit D deficiency disease. Bones become SOFT + DEFORMED (esp. in growing children — bowed legs, knock-knees, delayed walking, dental issues, weak teeth). VITAMIN D — chemical name CHOLECALCIFEROL (D3) or ERGOCALCIFEROL (D2). UNIQUE: synthesized in human SKIN when exposed to UV-B sunlight! Hence 'SUNSHINE VITAMIN.' SOURCES: (1) SUNLIGHT — most efficient (10-20 min sun exposure to face/arms 3-4×/week sufficient for most). (2) FATTY FISH (salmon, mackerel, sardines, tuna). (3) Egg yolk. (4) FORTIFIED milk + cereals. (5) Cod-liver oil. KEY ROLE: regulates CALCIUM + PHOSPHORUS absorption + bone mineralization. FUNCTION: liver converts D3 → 25(OH)D; kidneys → 1,25(OH)₂D (active form). DEFICIENCY: WIDESPREAD globally + in INDIA — ~70% Indians have low Vit D! Even sun-blessed countries have problem due to: (a) Indoor lifestyles (urban). (b) Sunscreen blocking UV-B. (c) Dark skin (less synthesis). (d) Pollution blocking UV. (e) Veiled clothing. SUPPLEMENTATION recommended for many. RDA: 600-800 IU/day adults; pregnancy/elderly more. EXCESS: rare hypercalcemia (kidney stones, calcification). KEY: RICKETS rare nowadays in developed countries due to milk fortification (USA since 1933). India: HIGH PREVALENCE despite sunshine — paradox. INDIAN GOVT: NATIONAL HEALTH POLICY recommends widespread Vit D screening + supplementation. UPSC angle: lifestyle disease + public health. PYQ FREQUENCY: rickets-Vit D in NEET, NCERT, SSC GA 1-2× per cycle.

questions.stem: BERIBERI disease is caused by deficiency of:
questions.explanation: BERIBERI — deficiency of VITAMIN B1 (THIAMINE). TWO TYPES: (1) WET BERIBERI — affects cardiovascular system; heart failure, edema (swelling). (2) DRY BERIBERI — affects nervous system; muscle weakness, paralysis (esp. legs). HISTORICAL: BERIBERI prevalent in Asian countries where POLISHED/REFINED RICE became staple — POLISHING removes thiamine-rich husk. ENDEMIC in Japan, Korea, Indonesia, parts of India (~late 1800s onwards). DISCOVERY of CAUSE: CHRISTIAAN EIJKMAN (Dutch, working in Java/Indonesia, 1890s) — observed chickens fed POLISHED rice developed beri-beri-like symptoms; rough rice cured them. Coined 'AVITAMINOSIS.' NOBEL 1929 (Eijkman + F. G. Hopkins). VITAMIN B1 = THIAMINE — chemically isolated 1926 by Jansen + Donath. Synthesized 1936. ROLE: COENZYME in CARBOHYDRATE METABOLISM (glycolysis, citric acid cycle); essential for nervous system + heart function. SOURCES: WHOLE GRAINS (brown rice, whole wheat, oats), pulses (beans, lentils), pork, sunflower seeds, fortified cereals. RDA: 1.1-1.2 mg/day. ALCOHOLISM linked to thiamine deficiency → WERNICKE-KORSAKOFF SYNDROME (memory loss, ataxia). MNEMONIC: 'B1 BeriBeri' — match initial letters. DON'T CONFUSE with: (1) RIBOFLAVIN (B2) — cheilosis. (2) NIACIN (B3) — pellagra (3 D's: Dermatitis, Diarrhea, Dementia). (3) PYRIDOXINE (B6) — anemia. (4) BIOTIN (B7) — skin/hair issues. (5) FOLATE (B9) — neural tube defects (very important in pregnancy!). (6) COBALAMIN (B12) — pernicious anemia. UPSC angle: nutrition policy. PYQ FREQUENCY: beriberi-thiamine in NEET, SSC GA 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: GOITRE (enlarged thyroid gland) is caused by deficiency of:
questions.explanation: GOITRE — enlarged thyroid gland; commonest cause is IODINE DEFICIENCY (NOT a vitamin — iodine is a TRACE MINERAL). Thyroid enlarges to capture more iodine when scarce. CAUSED BY: insufficient dietary iodine; thyroid produces less HORMONE → pituitary releases more TSH → thyroid grows trying to compensate. VITAMINS vs MINERALS: distinct categories of micronutrients. VITAMINS = organic; MINERALS = inorganic. KEY: IODINE is required for THYROID HORMONES (T3 — triiodothyronine, T4 — thyroxine) which regulate METABOLISM, growth, body temperature, brain development (esp. in fetus + early childhood). IODINE-DEFICIENCY DISORDERS (IDD): (1) GOITRE. (2) HYPOTHYROIDISM (sluggish metabolism, weight gain, fatigue). (3) CRETINISM (fetal/early-childhood iodine deficiency → severe mental + physical retardation; one of MOST COMMON preventable causes of intellectual disability globally). RDA: 150 µg/day; pregnancy/lactation more. SOURCES: IODIZED SALT (most reliable; mandated in INDIA since 2006), seafood (fish, prawn, seaweed), dairy, eggs, FRUITS+VEGETABLES grown in iodine-rich soil. INDIA — IODINE DEFICIENCY DISORDERS PROGRAMME (1962) → UNIVERSAL SALT IODIZATION (1992); MANDATORY since 2006. SUCCESS: GOITRE prevalence dropped from ~25% (1980s) to <5% in many areas. HIMALAYAN BELT, TARAI, COASTAL IODINE-DEFICIENT areas existed. WORLD IODINE DEFICIENCY DAY: 21 October. KEY HORMONES: T3 (~7%, but more potent), T4 (~93% of secretion). UPSC angle: micronutrient malnutrition + national programmes. PYQ FREQUENCY: goitre-iodine in NEET, NCERT, SSC GA 1× per cycle.

questions.explanation: VITAMIN K — essential for BLOOD CLOTTING. Required for synthesis of PROTHROMBIN (Factor II) + several other CLOTTING FACTORS (VII, IX, X, Proteins C + S). DEFICIENCY: PROLONGED BLEEDING from minor wounds, hemorrhage, easy bruising. VITAMIN K — chemically: PHYLLOQUINONE (K1, from plants) or MENAQUINONES (K2, from gut bacteria). DISCOVERY: HENRIK DAM (Danish, 1929) — Nobel 1943 (with E. Doisy who isolated structure). 'K' stands for 'KOAGULATION' (German, clotting). NATURAL SOURCES: (1) GREEN LEAFY VEGETABLES (spinach, kale, broccoli, lettuce, cabbage) — richest. (2) Vegetable oils (soybean, canola). (3) Some fruits. (4) GUT BACTERIA SYNTHESIZE Vit K2! (long-term antibiotics can cause deficiency by killing these bacteria). RDA: 90-120 µg/day. NEONATAL VITAMIN K: NEWBORNS deficient → Vit K SHOT given at birth (intramuscular) — prevents HEMORRHAGIC DISEASE OF NEWBORNS (HDN). Standard practice in India + globally. ANTICOAGULANT DRUGS: WARFARIN (rat poison + medical anticoagulant) works by INHIBITING Vit K cycle → reduces clotting. Used in patients at thrombosis risk; needs careful Vit K diet management. KEY: GREEN LEAFY VEGETABLES + GUT BACTERIA usually keep Vit K adequate. EXCESS not stored well; daily intake recommended. INDIAN CONTEXT: traditional diet high in greens; deficiency uncommon. NOBEL: HENRIK DAM 1943. CARL DAM HOENISBERG isolated Vit K2. UPSC angle: nutrition foundations + paediatric public health. PYQ FREQUENCY: Vit K-clotting in NEET, NCERT, SSC GA 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: PERNICIOUS ANEMIA + neurological problems are caused by deficiency of:
questions.explanation: VITAMIN B12 (COBALAMIN) — DEFICIENCY causes PERNICIOUS ANEMIA + NEUROLOGICAL DAMAGE (numbness, tingling, memory issues, severe cases — irreversible nerve damage). UNIQUE: B12 is the ONLY vitamin containing a METAL (cobalt, hence 'cobalamin'). MOLECULE is large + complex. ABSORPTION: requires INTRINSIC FACTOR (IF) — protein produced by stomach's parietal cells. AUTOIMMUNE attack on parietal cells → no IF → no B12 absorption → 'PERNICIOUS ANEMIA'. SOURCES: ANIMAL products ONLY — meat, fish, eggs, dairy. VEGANS at HIGH RISK; need supplements. PLANT foods: NEGLIGIBLE B12 (some claims for spirulina, fermented foods — not reliable). PRODUCED BY: bacteria (in some animals' gut, not humans'); humans must consume it. RDA: 2.4 µg/day; pregnancy/lactation more. KEY ROLES: (1) DNA SYNTHESIS — esp. in red blood cell production. (2) MYELIN sheath formation in nerves. (3) Methionine + folate metabolism. SYMPTOMS: fatigue, weakness, pale skin, sore tongue, numbness/tingling in extremities, memory issues, depression. INDIA — B12 DEFICIENCY: WIDESPREAD; ~70-80% of vegetarians (esp. Jains, strict Hindus) DEFICIENT! VEGETARIAN populations need supplementation. AYUSHMAN BHARAT health checks include B12 screening. STORAGE: liver stores ~2-5 years' worth; hence deficiency develops slowly. TREATMENT: oral or injectable B12; dietary changes for vegans. NOBEL: GEORGE WHIPPLE + GEORGE MINOT + WILLIAM MURPHY (1934) for liver-treatment of pernicious anemia. UPSC angle: VEGETARIAN nutrition + public health. PYQ FREQUENCY: B12 deficiency in NEET, AIIMS, NCERT 1× per cycle.
